title: The best way to "pump up" yourself (become smarter, more creative, and more successful) is to read books. Which ones?
text: **Start. Punch Fear In The Face, Escape Average and Do Work That Matters** **Author: John Acuff** A book about how to color your gray life in bright tones. Being like everyone else is the easiest thing to do. Being an unconventional person is a deed worthy of recognition. No matter how old you are, no matter what your social privileges are, it all comes down to one simple truth: you have to start. After reading this book, you will truly want to start taking action, start changing yourself and your life. And when better to start a new life than in the New Year? **This Year I Will… How to Finally Change a Habit, Keep Resolution, or Make a Dream Come True** **Author: M. J. Ryan** A book about how to change habits, keep promises, or fulfill long-held dreams. Usually, such life promises are made during the New Year, and after the holidays, they are successfully "forgotten". The book collects the author's knowledge in the fields of psychology, neurophysiology, and philosophy, which have translated into practical recommendations on how to fulfill promises made under the chimes. **Eat That Frog! 21 Great Ways to Stop Procrastinating and Get More Done in Less Time** **Author: Brian Tracy** A book about how to properly manage your time and solve difficult tasks by stepping out of your comfort zone. It contains 21 practical pieces of advice that can help you become as successful as the author. Brian Tracy is a millionaire who dropped out of school in his youth and started his path from scratch. This book is a compact and useful collection of Brian Tracy's personal effectiveness secrets. It has been translated into 40 languages and has a circulation of over 1,200,000 copies. **The Personal MBA. Master the Art of Business** **Author: Josh Kaufman** A book about self-education and self-belief. They are more important than academic degrees. The idea of the book is that there is no need to spend money on business school education. It is cheaper and more effective to engage in self-education, especially in the age of information technology. The book contains dozens of statements that teach a completely new business mindset. Josh Kaufman's advice is truly inspiring. The book can replace an MBA on many levels. **The Willpower Instinct** **Author: Kelly McGonigal** A book about becoming mentally strong, resisting temptations, and stopping procrastination. The book exudes scientific rigor. All the advice is backed by numerous psychological and medical studies. That is why the book is useful not only for those in need of strengthening their willpower, but also for curious people who will find plenty of interesting insights.

title: 6 rules for achieving success in life
text: 1. Law of Mirror. The people around me reflect my own personality, sometimes even aspects of it that I don't think about. For example, if someone is rude to me, it means that I am also ready to show rudeness in my heart. Therefore, there is no need to be offended by others. 2. Law of Choice. I realize that everything that happens in my life is a result of my own choice, based on my feelings and sensations. Therefore, I have no reason to blame anyone else. The authorship of my destiny belongs only to me. 3. Law of Responsibility. I am willing to take responsibility for my decisions and abandon excuses that do not bring anything. 4. Law of Mistakes. I acknowledge the fallibility of my opinions and judgments. Stubbornly clinging to one's own rightness will eventually lead to personal catastrophe. Those who insist on being right do not see reality. 5. Law of Correspondence. In my life, I have exactly what I deserve and as much as I truly correspond to. This applies to relationships, roles, and financial position. Therefore, all my complaints are meaningless. When I change my attitude towards the world around me, circumstances also change. 6. Law of Presence - "Here and Now". The past is gone, and it no longer exists. The future doesn't exist yet either. The inclination to pity the past leads to depression, worrying about the future breeds anxiety. As long as I am alive, I am immortal. This is a reason to rejoice.

title: How entrepreneurs think
text: The majority of people spend money on basic necessities, entertainment, and other needs. Entrepreneurs, however, spend money with the goal of earning even more. Thus, the main difference between the rich and the poor lies in their habits. What habits do entrepreneurs have that others do not? Let's consider an ordinary lottery winner in this context. Most of them will spend their millions within a few years, as their goal is to spend money on their own pleasure and improving their lives. When a person buys a house, they buy the most expensive one their money can afford. If their salary increases, they immediately need to buy a new car. And when they don't have enough money, regular people take out loans. For an entrepreneur, such behavior seems absurd. Money is merely a means of earning. For example, Warren Buffett and his friend, during their second year of university, bought a used arcade machine for $25 and turned it into a profitable source of income. Regular teenagers wouldn't have done that. Everything else stems from this principle. **1. Financial prudence.** An aspiring entrepreneur saves their profits to increase their income. It is easy to recognize an aspiring entrepreneur who is not succeeding - they spend a lot of money. And even after reaching wealth, most businessmen still live frugally. They may spend a lot, but always less than what they earn. **2. Developing skills that have a synergistic effect.** The entrepreneur views their skills as investments. If time is spent, it must bring profits. Entrepreneurs typically are self-taught and hardworking. They work on themselves and become people who achieve wealth. **3. Assets must also work together.** Working alone will not make one rich. Entrepreneurs quickly realize that it is most profitable to own a company, as their efforts are multiplied by the efforts of subordinates. Bill Gates, perhaps, was a good programmer, but alone, he would never have earned $50 billion. Therefore, smart entrepreneurs strive for shares in companies. **4. Conscious time and attention management.** Time and attention are our only truly limited resources. They are very easy to waste. Successful entrepreneurs keenly feel this and are usually highly organized, intolerant of inefficiency, and focused on the task at hand. Many well-known businessmen wear the same clothes every day, claiming that there is no time to waste on choosing. **5. Positive realism.** To make the right decisions - because they are what make people wealthy - it is necessary to accurately assess the odds. Life can sometimes be unpleasant, difficult, and confusing, and it is not always easy to see its brighter side. But when full information is unavailable, it is better to look at the world from a positive perspective. Pessimists never become successful entrepreneurs.

title: How to achieve completion of what has been started, regardless of everything
text: **1. Make a to-do list.** Take a pen and paper, open a special app or program, and right now make a list of all the things that are pressing on you. Take 10 minutes to relax, as you have already expressed everything that bothers you on paper/screen. Go back to the list, look at it critically: which of the listed reasons is preventing you from completing each of the mentioned tasks? **2. Remove the unnecessary.** Read the list again. Think about how necessary these macrame courses are, to which you were forced to enroll because of your bored friend? And will these books help you in your career? Delete tasks that are not feasible. Better spend time on something really important. **3. Remember the "two-minute rule".** In time management, there is a principle called the "two-minute rule": tasks that take no more than 2-5 minutes are done immediately and removed. Organizing a shelf in the closet, tidying up a shelf in the bathroom, loading the washing machine with laundry - all of this takes no more than 5 (maximum 10) minutes. Just half an hour has passed, and you have already accomplished 5-10 tasks! **4. Become French - eat the "frog".** Highlight in green all the items on the list that you haven't completed due to laziness. These are the most unpleasant tasks that you postpone until the last minute, in time management they are called "frogs". Deal with such unpleasant tasks better in the morning. For example, you need to write a commercial proposal to potential clients. Imagine in detail how you will write it, send it, and how potential clients become the most loyal ones. Feel it, do it, and then spend the rest of the day on enjoyable activities. **5. Divide the "elephant".** Complex and difficult tasks are called "elephants". If you don't know where to start, try dividing the task into several stages or subtasks. The simpler and faster a stage is completed, the better. What will your mind perceive easier: 5 difficult and time-consuming tasks or 20 simple tasks that take 5 minutes each? The main rule is to come back to the tasks when you have a free minute. Suppose you have decided to learn French. In the morning, you learned one grammar rule, during the day - 10 words, in the evening you composed several sentences with new words according to the learned rule. Soon you will be able to communicate effectively with your French business partners. **6. Praise yourself.** There is nothing that can bring you more joy and inspiration than a long list of completed tasks. So, as soon as you finish a task, confidently cross it out and be sure to reward yourself for it. Your enthusiasm will increase if there is some form of reward for your efforts: shopping, a pleasant evening, a delicious treat with tea. **7. Sum up.** Set aside a few hours once a week or month (depending on your convenience) to summarize. You will notice that many tasks have been completed, a few "frogs" have disappeared, and a couple of "elephants" are still left undone. Once again, praise yourself and add new tasks to the list.

title: What not to do if your income suddenly increases?
text: When our income suddenly increases, it is a reason to rejoice. However, the wrong attitude towards a sudden increase in income can lead to a catastrophic shortage of funds after some time. To avoid this, it is enough to observe a few rules. 1. Do not buy things impulsively, based on "mood" or just because you have enough money. Buy only what was planned in a calm state. Then these things will continue to bring you joy with their practicality. 2. Try to gradually and responsibly get used to the "new money," living on the "old amount" for some time. Divide the income into two parts: the amount you were receiving before the income increase, and the amount that has been added. Spend the old amount on necessary expenses such as transportation, food, utilities, and loan payments. As for the "addition," it is recommended to follow this plan: - Put 50% into a high-yield bank deposit. This will allow you to accumulate a significant capital. According to experts' calculations, by investing just 150 rubles a day (the cost of a cup of coffee in a well-known coffee shop), you can have millions in a few years. - Spend 20% on purchasing a new suit or phone to match your new position (or save it for the future). - Allocate 10% to a charitable fund or financially assist those in need among acquaintances and relatives. 3. Do not show off your financial well-being. Do not strive to buy a multitude of "status" items. Functionally, they are no different from ordinary things, they just cost much more. 4. Do not take on new loans without paying off the previous ones. Even if you believe that you can afford any loan right now. However, this euphoria can be deceptive, and you may underestimate your financial capabilities.

title: The thinking of a successful person
text: Every person is born for happiness. Absolutely everyone. And only our own attitude towards life, our thoughts, affect whether we feel happy and believe in our ability to achieve success. It is our thinking that determines where and how we are moving. Most people believe that successful people always have luck on their side, that they have a good start - inheritance, wealthy parents, in a word, a good initial capital. Certainly, there are such cases. But far from all people who have achieved significant success in life started with a substantial sum of money. Among successful people, there are many who have experienced numerous failures and even bankruptcy. This only confirms that it is not about the starting capital. The main secret of any successful person is their thinking, which fundamentally differs from the thinking of losers. 1. Successful people are positive. They always enjoy life, despite all obstacles. They can find the good in almost everything. It is always pleasant to communicate with them because they are cheerful and friendly. Such people are literally infectious with their positivity. 2. Successful people believe in themselves and in their success. They never tell themselves "I won't succeed at anything," because they are already predisposed to exert maximum efforts to make everything work out. But even if something doesn't work out, they, unlike losers, ask themselves "How and what can I do in this situation?" and look for ways to achieve positive results. 3. Successful people are not afraid of mistakes because they understand that only those who do nothing make no mistakes. Mistakes provide experience, and experience is the most valuable acquisition. 4. Successful people never seek excuses for their inaction. They understand perfectly well that excuses are of no interest to anyone. Only results matter. 5. Successful people are always honest with themselves. If they lack the knowledge or experience to solve a particular task, they are capable of admitting it and are not afraid to seek help. If they are overwhelmed by fear, they find the strength within themselves to overcome it and act further. 6. Successful people are persistent in achieving their goals, perceiving any difficulties not as problems but as tasks that need to be solved. 7. Successful people are not afraid of responsibility. They make decisions independently, even if these decisions contradict the opinions of others. 8. Successful people know that the best investment is an investment in themselves, in their development, education, and health. Meanwhile, losers prefer to buy another trinket instead of a useful book. 9. Successful people do not fixate on what has become outdated (work, business, relationships, etc.). They do not try to ride a dead horse in the hope of reviving it. 10. Successful people are always IN favor of mutually beneficial partnership. They understand that building relationships based on mutual benefit contributes to long-term cooperation. 11. And finally, successful people are always active. They prefer to take action and make full use of the opportunities available to them. As you can see, everything depends on the attitude towards a particular situation, towards life itself. Think positively. Smile at life – and life will definitely smile back at you.

title: How to develop business thinking
text: Business thinking is a tool for attracting clients. The better it is developed in an entrepreneur, the more clients he can attract. This helps the entrepreneur see many opportunities for making money. Its development is beneficial for both beginners and experienced businessmen who strive for constant growth in sales and profits. Business thinking as a success factor Where an ordinary person sees obstacles and problems, a businessman sees an opportunity to increase his capital, create new sources of growth. The development of business thinking is necessary for everyone who is engaged in or intends to engage in business. It is not a given at birth, so it needs to be developed. The better it is developed, the more success can be achieved. If an entrepreneur has not developed business thinking, he faces either the "specialist syndrome" or the "life syndrome". The specialist syndrome is when a businessman does business while remaining essentially a specialist in a particular field. The life syndrome is when a businessman conducts business based on his subjective worldview. The main skill of a businessman is attracting clients. A person with developed business thinking does this easily and naturally. If a person has not developed it, then he is not a businessman, but simply a specialist in a specific field and relies on someone to bring him clients or they will find him on their own. The specialist believes that his task is to do the work. A specialist cannot attract clients, he can only serve them. He experiences the "specialist syndrome," which in 99% of cases leads to bankruptcy. Specialists believe that there are many ready-made clients who will find them on their own. While they think so, true businessmen actively attract clients and leave specialists without work. An ordinary person is also incapable of attracting clients. He can only communicate on a human level. Accordingly, in cases where it is necessary to behave like a businessman and earn money, he behaves like an ordinary person. He believes that it is enough to just communicate with the client to interest him. At this time, true businessmen actively attract clients. Business, in its essence, has a certain idea. In fact, business is simply the embodiment of this idea. Only someone in whom it is "implanted" and who has honed it well can implement it. The person who has honed the idea best is capable of creating the most effective business. Overcoming the "specialist syndrome" and the "life syndrome" involves the implementation of the idea and its deep honing. Business thinking is developed through the implementation of the business idea and its honing using the business grammar methodology or the "Immersion in Business" training. However, it is not enough to just implement the business idea. It is also necessary to have a good understanding of the market, for which the idea of the market needs to be honed. The implementation of the market idea and its honing is done through the market grammar methodology. The most advanced businessmen are those with the most developed business thinking. They see opportunities that are unnoticed by others, and this is what allows them to make money where others cannot. Anyone can become an advanced businessman after developing business thinking. Anyone who makes an effort can become an effective businessman.

title: Why Start a Business from the End
text: What unites a tightrope walker and an entrepreneur? Both must maintain balance in difficult conditions. However, there is also what sets them apart. This is their attitude towards risk. The path of a tightrope walker is dangerous. And it is hardly possible to find a daredevil who would dare to cross the height without training and without insurance. But among beginner businessmen, there are plenty of such brave ones. Perhaps, if their life depended on every step of an entrepreneur, businesses would less often fall into the abyss. In business, as in balancing, two principles are important: - The principle of balance. - The principle of insurance. With the right ratio of income and expenses, a business becomes balanced and provides itself with profit. Profit is the balancing pole of your business. Without profit, a business loses stability. Nothing disciplines like thoughts of profit. You start investing wisely and growing sensibly. But the most important thing: thoughts of profit will lead you to what business starts with - sales. The volume of sales depends on costs and the profit rate. It is useful to understand what figures are involved at the approach to your business: - How much will you spend per month on maintaining an office (store, cafe, production): on rent and utilities, banking services, internet and telephony, software and hardware support? - How much per month will you spend on maintaining employees: on recruiting and training staff, tax payments, and wages? - How much will you invest monthly in advertising and promoting your business? The calculations made will give an idea of: - What markup percentage you need to enter the market and make a profit. - What sales volume you need for breakeven. - How many customers you will need to meet the sales plan. - How many employees will be required to attract/retain this number of customers. The answers to these questions will convince you that sales are not only a result but also a process that requires constant care. And business should start with them. Uncontrolled sales make business spontaneously unpredictable. No sales - no profit - no business. First, start counting, and then start a business.

title: What is the need for risk in business?
text: By taking risks, we reveal our hidden potential, which gives us momentum and success in business development. Risk is a masculine element. Developing our business, providing for our families, making business deals - all of this requires determination and the ability to make necessary decisions, which is associated with risk. However, many people are afraid to take risks and take responsibility for a business failure or financial setback. Very often, those who hold high positions and manage huge corporations impeccably and boldly make serious and responsible decisions. But when it comes to their own funds, they carefully avoid any risk. The desire and willingness to take risks, especially in business, is a necessary condition for those who want to achieve high incomes. Of course, it is also important to consider that the safety of ourselves and our loved ones always comes first. We must be able to see and assess the value of this risk. But if you don't understand a particular project, it does not mean that it is not serious or that there is some deception involved. On the contrary, you simply need to study the information about the project in which you are investing and possibly acquire the necessary knowledge to understand it. Risk optimization in business. Spread your risk. For example, do not invest all your money in one place. Let's say you have several investments in different projects. There is no perfect and ideal project. Rather, it exists, but we can only find out how profitable our investment was when we look back and evaluate it. If we look into the future, we still cannot know what awaits us. Therefore, waiting for the perfect project in investments is not always reasonable. You just need to start! Since you will never know how accurately you have evaluated a particular investment. And of course, someday, you will still lose some money. Show me a person who never makes mistakes. No matter how much you would like, there will be losses, it is better to have them at the beginning of your business. Only then will you understand that these losses are not so devastating. And despite all this, you will still achieve the income you want. Safety of risks in business! Those who strive to perfectly secure themselves from risks and problems will not achieve the expected result. They observe others, expect something, consult with someone, constantly study something... But it is better to start with mistakes than to doubt perfectly. There will come a moment when you will definitely find yourself in a situation where your risk will be very high, and you will do everything to stay ahead and not lose what you have. And under certain circumstances, you won't even forgive yourself for missing out on a wonderful opportunity just because you weren't ready to take a risk. After all, our life is made up of actions and decisions that we have to constantly make. Many crucial moments in our lives are determined by the decisions we did not make and the moments we missed, did not notice in time. Of course, many of us do not take risks because it is associated with the fear of failure. But this feeling also has another side - it helps us seek other solutions, choose options, and fear helps us understand, teaches us, develops patience and endurance. The good news is that these qualities are not innate, they appear over time and with experience. "A sailboat in a calm harbor is much safer, but it is not made for that." We often come across these words on the Internet, but we rarely think about the current situation in our rapidly changing world, and failures are only guaranteed when you stay in one place and do not leave the shore. We are afraid to take risks to forever change our lives for the better.

title: Top 10 characteristics of a promising business concept
text: **1. The creator is fully passionate about the idea. ** If you are pursuing the idea solely for profit, it makes sense to stop right away. Money can be a good motivator, but you need to be prepared for periodic difficulties in entrepreneurship. To assess your commitment to the idea, ask yourself: Can you imagine yourself working on it ten years from now? **2. The idea is simple. ** Big ideas grow, they don't appear big right away. There was no moment when Mark Zuckerberg suddenly said, "I will create the biggest social network in the world." All great companies of our time started with something very simple (for example, Google began with organizing library books). **3. The idea is easily explainable. ** When an entrepreneur starts their business, they often spend a lot of time explaining what they are going to do (the audience can be diverse - from potential clients to potential investors). If the founder cannot explain the essence of their project in 10 words, the chances of success are extremely low. It's worth starting with solving one problem, one product. **4. One source of income. ** A startup must be very successful to find one powerful source of income, not to mention three or four. Therefore, in the beginning, it is advisable to focus on one source and put all efforts into it. **5. Few steps to profit. ** The more steps there are before you can start earning income, the more people need to help to make the business stable. However, the path to profit for successful projects is short enough. **6. Knowing your customers. ** First, it is necessary to carefully study the type of consumer who needs your product. Besides, there is no person you would know better than yourself! Remember how many successful projects were born because the creators wanted to satisfy their own needs. **7. Knowing the market. ** How can you know market trends and predict the future without becoming an expert in a specific field? If you are not an expert yet, it's time to become one. **8. A sufficiently extensive market. ** Any market covering less than 10 million people will be quite difficult to capture - it's not worth investing time and effort. It is too difficult to win on a small market - you need to think on a large scale. **9. An original secret ingredient. ** Are you doing something unique? Are you doing something better than everyone else? Do you know a secret that no one else possesses? **10. Share your idea. ** It is unlikely that anyone dreams of quitting everything and suddenly devoting their life to realizing your idea. Get feedback from as many people as possible - don't be afraid to share.

title: 20 signs that you can become a successful entrepreneur
text: Entrepreneurs are a special group of people who not only possess a distinctive way of thinking but also take unique actions. Generating ideas that lie at the intersection of madness and genius, these individuals rely on unparalleled personal traits, habits, and intellectual abilities. But don't think that being a talented inventor with a concept for replacing gasoline with alternative fuel makes you capable of becoming an entrepreneur. If you have ever wondered if you belong to the aforementioned group of people, compare the traits of your personality and behavior with the items on the following list. You may not possess all the characteristics, but having at least some of them is an indicator of having an entrepreneurial streak. **1. Your relatives have never worked for someone else** Your parents were engaged in their own business. However, this statement does not apply to all entrepreneurs: some people from such families were wage workers. **2. You can't stand the current situation** You always question why people do what they do. You strive to improve everything within your capabilities and are willing to make efforts for that. **3. You believe in yourself** Have you ever seen an entrepreneur who was pessimistic about themselves? Indeed, if you don't believe in yourself, how will others believe in you? Most entrepreneurs evaluate themselves only positively. **4. You are a passionate person** During the course of doing business, there may be a situation where you spend a lot of time and energy but don't make money. In such a situation, only your passion will allow you to keep going. **5. You don't take no for an answer** An entrepreneur never gives up. Never. **6. You are good at building business relationships with strangers** People are generally attracted to you because of your charm. Mostly because of your passion. **7. You spend more time with your business partner than with your life partner** **8. You dropped out of school like Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, and Mark Zuckerberg** **9. Every morning, you go to your office — from the bedroom to the living room** **10. You have always been considered a failure and have probably been fired several times** Don't worry, you are not alone. It doesn't reflect poorly on you. Perhaps you are just not meant for employment. **11. You are always against authority** That's why you couldn't stay in one job for long. **12. You have job security** You understand that you are not at risk of unemployment as long as you control the situation and don't rely on a boss who can destroy your career at any moment. **13. Most of your clothing consists of t-shirts** And, let's be honest, they are not from the most expensive brands. Perhaps they have inscriptions related to your interests or your company logo. **14. You are a persistent person** You always know that you can do something better. **15. You check GitHub every morning** **16. You accept payment in tickets to matches, shoes, or other items that you love** After all, there is something better than money, right? **17. Your ideal day off is a work day without distractions** **18. You can't find a job** This is not a bad thing. Life skills are more valuable than corporate culture. **19. You work more than 60 hours a week** While earning more than in school. **20. You want to be both the leader and the executor in your company** Generally, you prefer to control all the processes related to the functioning of your company.

title: 7 deadly sins of any business
text: 1. Irresponsibility: an irresponsible individual is dangerous and uncontrollable, they are no different from someone mentally ill or mentally unhealthy. Trusting them with something is foolish, explaining is like talking to a wall. They are the most dangerous individual in the business. 2. Negligence is a sign of disrespect towards the work and colleagues. 3. Lack of punctuality: inability to manage one's time leads to consequences that affect the overall result. Everyone starts to suffer. Delaying responsibilities leads to missing deadlines, which is equivalent to not doing the job at all. Being late for meetings, appointments, conferences, shows disrespect towards oneself and colleagues. 4. Weakness of character: fear of taking responsibility, fear of making decisions independently, whining and evading make the individual useless in the business. Such people cannot be trusted, they can let you down in difficult times. 5. title: 6 financial principles that will help you achieve a comfortable life quickly
text: **1. Invest in yourself.** Education, training, and more. Self-development and learning are reliable paths to success and prosperity. **2. Consider the rule of three eights.** It is well known that on average we work 8 hours, sleep 8 hours, and have another 8 hours of personal time between these activities. We give our working hours to someone else, and the hours spent sleeping take care of our bodies. Therefore, the only way to grow and improve our lives is to use these remaining eight hours between work and sleep wisely. **3. Be cautious when providing loans to relatives and close ones.** It is possible that someone you know or a relative secretly believes that you are favorable to them and that debt forgiveness is possible after some time. Therefore, it is important to negotiate in advance about the exact repayment terms. **4. Save more, and you will gain freedom of action and flexibility.** By starting to save on things that are not important to you, you are not hurting yourself - you are gaining flexibility and freedom of action. You are buying the opportunity to change jobs, move to another place, and prioritize what truly matters. **5. Always spend 1 minute analyzing expenses.** This trick is surprisingly simple, but it allows you to control your expenses every day and prevent unnecessary spending due to absent-mindedness. Closer to the midday, spend just one minute checking and reflecting on the financial transactions you have already made. title: How to learn to express your thoughts elegantly?

title: Rules for multiplying wealth
text: How many assets do you need to be considered wealthy - this is a purely individual question and depends on the personal preferences of each person. However, when we talk about multiplying wealth, we definitely mean growth of wealth, some increase. So, let's consider important rules for multiplying wealth. Rule 1. Save, don't spend. All expenses on personal needs do not contribute to the multiplication of a person's wealth, even if it's hundreds of thousands or millions of monetary units. Because wealth is what remains, not what is spent. Therefore, the first and most important rule for multiplying wealth is to not spend, but to save and accumulate as much of your income as possible. It is the saved money and material assets that form wealth. It is necessary to set aside at least 10% of your income, but the more portion of your income you save, the faster your wealth will multiply. People who successfully accumulate wealth usually save at least half of their income. Rule 2. Money should work. If you simply save money without investing them, they will gradually depreciate due to inflation. Therefore, money should be invested in assets, preferably income-generating ones, which preserve finances from inflation and increase them. In other words, you need to invest. By saving money to create new money, you create your personal capital - the most important financial asset. Of course, it is also necessary to acquire spending assets for life, such as real estate and a car, but only considering the ability to maintain them without significant financial difficulties. These assets are also part of wealth. When investing, it is important to remember about risks and diversification. In simpler terms, "don't put all your eggs in one basket," but this is a very superficial judgment. Rule 3. Pay yourself first! Where do you get the money to invest? It is important to save money immediately, following this important rule for multiplying wealth. If you save money at the end, according to the "remainder" principle, wealth accumulation will be much less effective, as the remainder will be small or even zero. It is very important to pay yourself first, creating wealth, and then others: sellers of goods and services that you acquire for your life needs.

title: 4 main questions about finances that you need to know the answers to
text: 1. What is the amount of your debt? To quickly deal with debts, it is necessary to know exactly how much you owe. It is also important to understand how much time it will take to repay them. Without this, it is impossible to develop a clear repayment plan, which is necessary. Calculate how many years and months it will take to repay the debts, and when you can start increasing the payments. If you are in a long-term relationship, it is important to know how much debt your partner has, as this also affects you. 2. How much savings do you have? This will help you understand how much you spend and how much you save, as well as plan your emergency fund. If you have accumulated a sufficient amount for several months, consider transferring it to retirement savings, investments, or other major goals. This is especially important to know if you plan budgeting together with your spouse. Having a clear understanding of your financial amount is the first step towards financial independence. 3. What is your debt and the interest rate on your credit card? You probably rarely calculate in cash. It is much more convenient to use cards or applications now. However, this can lead to overspending and getting into debt. Do not forget to monitor the balance of your credit card every month. Set up SMS notifications or check the balance daily in the banking application. To maintain a good credit history, try not to spend more than 30% of your limit and repay the debt within a month. If you are unable to pay off the credit card debt within a month, it is important to know how much interest will be charged to you. This will help you make a decision about which debt to repay first and which card to use in unexpected situations. 4. How much do you want to earn? Do not forget that money is not the most important thing. However, your earnings depend on many factors that you cannot control. It is not worth dedicating your whole life to earning money. However, it is important to set goals and strive to achieve them. Knowing the required amount makes it easier to make decisions about your career. Think about what you are working for. If you strive for financial independence, you need to earn and save a certain amount. This will allow you to retire earlier or start your own business. If you work to support your family, your income should be sufficient to meet all family needs. Define the amount you aim for, but do not get too fixated on strict limits. It's okay if you don't reach your ideal amount down to the exact date. There are always factors that are beyond your control.

title: Four things that kill meeting productivity
text: Business meetings have acquired a reputation as a useless activity that wastes precious time. According to a Harvard Business Review study, 65% of senior managers believe that meetings hinder their work, and 71% consider meetings unproductive and ineffective. The author of the book "How to Conduct Effective, Interesting, and Enjoyable Meetings" Maimi Kanfer Stewart believes that meeting productivity suffers from the following factors. **You do not verbalize decisions made.** Many meetings end with the words "Perhaps we have found a solution to the problem," but does everyone understand what decision has been reached? "There is no unified 'we'; not everyone is willing to take responsibility and take the next necessary steps," Stewart believes. "Most likely, everyone at the meeting has their own idea of what needs to be done next, and after the meeting, everyone will go their separate ways with different decisions." The meeting leader should say the following: "Perhaps we need to solve the problem in the following way. Is everyone clear? Can someone repeat and write down what we ultimately decided on?" Employees can suggest different ideas, but someone needs to verbalize and record specific decisions made. **You invite too many people.** When you invite employees to a meeting, sometimes the "fear of missing out" syndrome arises, and you invite absolutely everyone. But because of the large number of employees, the meeting can become unproductive. It is better to discuss some details with a few people before the meeting, and then inform those gathered about them. Or have someone comment on the decisions made by email. If you have been invited to a meeting where you feel you are not needed, ask the person who invited you what they expect from you. Explain that you are not trying to avoid attending meetings, but rather want to optimize your time. **You do not write down important points.** Some organizations appoint a specific person to record the key points of the meeting. But more often than not, this important task is forgotten. Meeting notes should not look like minutes of a court session, but they should also not contain anything unnecessary. "People will read your notes only if they are concise and relevant," Stewart believes. "If you do not record the conclusions, you force people to attend the meeting simply because otherwise they will not know what important things happened there." **You do not adhere to the corporate culture.** A meeting is a good opportunity to let employees feel the corporate culture, but this rarely happens. For example, if you discuss everything openly but do not send anyone the meeting outcomes. Generally, such meetings go poorly because they are organized incorrectly. "When you give people freedom in meetings, you get rid of bureaucracy," Stewart believes. "Some leaders allow their employees to argue, while others think it is inappropriate. But if each meeting follows different rules, people start to get tired." Pay special attention to the people who conduct meetings and the methods they use. But this does not mean that all meetings with employees should always follow the same pattern - for example, a weekly meeting will differ from a company-wide gathering. Think about how to develop a course of action for the project and how to outline the subsequent steps. Use appropriate tools for this, such as Word, Google Docs, or specialized planners.

title: What to do if you encounter a deadlock
text: Regardless of what you are doing - developing a skill, building a business, sooner or later your progress will slow down. And no matter how hard you try, the result will not come. It may even seem like you are moving backwards. Here's what you need to do in such a situation. **1. Understand that it's a good thing.** In nature, healthy progress happens over time. For example, when it gets cold, trees and animals go into hibernation, waiting for warmer weather. The same goes for human achievements. At different times, you will move forward at a great speed, and sometimes you will crawl like a snail. The fact that you have reached a plateau means that your success is natural and sustainable, and it is not an artificial bubble that will soon burst. **2. Believe in yourself.** Even if it seems like you are stuck, the mere fact that you have come this far proves that you can go further. Get inspired and find the source of your motivation, the goal that drives you in the right direction. Understand why you are pursuing this goal, why it is worth it, even when it seems like your efforts are not being rewarded. **3. Continue to focus on the main current tasks.** Thomas Edison said that genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration. Sweating means waking up every day and practicing the core skills and tasks. This is what athletes and entrepreneurs do. It is the daily attention to details that ultimately pays off. **4. Acknowledge your deadlock.** It may seem like you have fallen into a pit - you are practicing the fundamentals, but it seems like everything is getting worse. Fewer successful deals, wider winnings for competitors you easily defeated before. It is during these moments that many people give up: it seems absolutely hopeless. But don't give up. Yes, it is worth even noting this moment, because failures are a clear signal that your progress on the plateau is coming to an end. And you are close to the next step, to... **5. Experience a breakthrough.** If, when in a deadlock, you do not lose your determination, you will make an important discovery, grasp an idea that will allow you to reach a new level. As long as you continue to hope, dream, as long as you are focused on your craft, a breakthrough is inevitable. It will happen.

title: Help for aspiring entrepreneurs

title: How not to lose your potential
text: Quite often you can hear that some people have great potential. However, not everyone will be able to fulfill it. To do this right, you need to determine your goals and put maximum effort into achieving them. **Look for motivation.** If you want to unleash your potential, you need to make a reasonable choice in favor of personal growth. Tell yourself that you are ready to change and develop, it will help you rapidly grow towards your goal. To get additional motivation, you can read various books and attend seminars dedicated to self-development, or communicate with people who share your worldview. **Set goals.** Developing potential without a specific goal is meaningless. Focus your attention on something significant to you, on the things you want to achieve in the near future. Perhaps you dream of becoming a successful entrepreneur or a renowned athlete. However, remember that every person is a unique individual, and there are no universal ways to unleash potential. Look for goals that genuinely interest you, that are important to you at present, and that you can achieve in the future. **Don't give up and work systematically.** The goal you set for yourself may seem unattainable. You may have doubts about its achievability. Your task is to fight such thoughts and move forward, solving all the tasks that arise before you. By doing so, you will prove to yourself that you are capable of resolving the most challenging problems. For example, if you decide to go to the gym, you may have doubts about whether you will ever be able to lift a 100 kg barbell. Your task is to start small, make regular workouts a habit, and then move forward, gradually increasing the weight. In this way, step by step, you will unleash your potential. **Record achievements.** Lack of self-confidence, as well as a lack of motivation, often arise from a person not seeing the dynamics of changes in their achievements. Keep a diary or open a blog on the internet. Write down all your successes there, regardless of how significant they are. For example, "Did 50 push-ups", "Attracted the first 10 clients", or "Lost 10 kg" and so on. Every time you have doubts about the correctness of your actions, reread your notes, remind yourself that you have already achieved great results. **Set an example for yourself.** When developing your potential, never compare yourself to other people. It is pointless, as there will always be those who have greater successes in the same field, as well as those who lag behind you. Focus on your abilities, set new goals, and continue to develop, without paying attention to others.

title: Not stingy, but benefit from it
text: It is not a secret that our words influence our thoughts and our lives, including the presence or absence of money. title: Key principles of personnel management
text: Forget what you learned from specialized literature on personnel management. In fact, there is only one way to ensure that each of your subordinates will be an outstanding employee. Not all books on personnel management touch on this topic. Most of them try to teach you how to manage "people". Simply managing "people" is impossible. Due to the individuality of each person, a method that works for one may be ineffective for another. Certain employees succeed when they are publicly praised, while others thrive when they are specifically distinguished. Some depend on salary, while others value challenging and engaging projects. Some require a mentor for constant support, while advice annoys others. The key idea is to manage personnel according to their own desires, rather than based on your skills or convenience. The only way to find out is to ask. In your first (or next) meeting with them, ask the following questions: What can I do to make it even more convenient for you to work? What will help you become more effective? What aspects of management irritate you? Listen carefully to their answers and adapt your methods to each employee. By the way, some employees won't expect you to ask them these questions - they may directly tell you what would be better and more convenient for them at work. And when that happens - don't forget to take note of it!

text: 1. Preparation. Preparing for business... It's a special state... When you understand that you desire this, or have decided that you want to work for yourself. title: Professional Marketing as a Guarantee of Success
text: Professional marketing is a versatile tool that ensures business growth. There is also the concept of amateur self-marketing, which is a factor in the decline in trade activity, which in turn reduces demand. The main idea of self-marketing is the hypothesis that a product can sell itself. The final product automatically creates demand for itself and the need to purchase it. Therefore, it is logical to assume that such a product can give itself value and generate profits based on its sales. At the same time, it should be remembered that the demand for such a product will be limited and probably not very high. Marketers note that the need for such a product practically tends to zero, while the demand remains at a minimum acceptable level. Accordingly, with low demand, sales will be low. The process of self-marketing is quite simple. For example, there is a company that produces a product, and then the end consumer purchases it and begins to use it for specific purposes. During the use of the product, the consumer experiences positive and negative emotions. These emotions reflect the idea of the product. Thus, the consumer enters into close contact with the idea of the product, starting to evaluate and criticize it. Then, all judgments about the product are transmitted from one consumer to another. Therefore, this is how the marketing of the product is launched. The first consumer shares impressions and emotions with his surroundings. Usually, a person has about 20-100 people around him. That is, potentially, another 20-100 people can learn about the product. If the majority of emotions among people are negative, then the product is unlikely to be purchased. In the case of positive emotions, the sales of the discussed product may increase. Thus, self-marketing is achieved when the product promotes itself. Experts in the field of entrepreneurship note that such a scheme will not work if the main goal of any business is to maximize profits. Hence, it can be said that more detailed marketing is needed to increase sales. Product marketing does not work because consumer tastes, preferences, income levels, and other indicators change. This means that in the first month, he may be satisfied with the product, but then it will evoke negative emotions. The problem of self-marketing would be solved if there was only one product on the market, but such a phenomenon does not exist in a market economy. Therefore, entrepreneurs need detailed marketing with the study of consumer preferences, defining the target audience for the product, and pricing policy.

title: How to develop self-discipline
text: Certainly many of you have weak self-discipline. Perhaps some of you currently cannot do certain things that you would like to do – for example, play the guitar. You can develop self-discipline in a similar way to how you increase your muscle mass. It may take not only one week or one month but, ultimately, you will make significant progress. **1. Self-awareness.** Discipline is the ability to act according to your convictions, regardless of the current state. Therefore, the first component of self-discipline is self-reflection. Determine what behavior best reflects your goals and values. This process requires self-analysis, and it is best to do it in writing. Make time to write down your goals, dreams, and ambitions. It is especially useful to create a mission statement – this will help you better understand yourself and what you value. **2. Mindfulness.** Self-discipline depends on awareness of your actions and inactions. Think about it. How can you correct your behavior if you are not aware that it is undisciplined? When you start developing self-discipline, you notice your undisciplined actions: biting your nails, skipping workouts, eating a piece of cake, or constantly checking your e-book. Developing self-discipline takes time, and a key aspect of this process is becoming aware of your undisciplined behavior. Over time, you will notice this awareness earlier before getting into an undisciplined situation. **3. Commitment to self-discipline.** It is not enough to simply write down your goals and values. You must set internal commitments for yourself. Otherwise, when the alarm clock goes off at 5 o'clock in the morning, it will be difficult for you to make the decision to get up and start acting right away. Or when the initial enthusiasm fades, you will postpone your project without completing it. If you hesitate in your commitment, consciously make the decision that you must fulfill what you committed to - in that very moment and in the same way you planned. Follow the advice to track your commitments. As they say, "what can be measured can be improved." **4. Courage.** Do not set yourself overly difficult tasks. Mood, desire, and passion can become powerful obstacles. That is why self-discipline requires courage. Do not deceive yourself by saying that what is actually difficult or painful is easy to do. Instead, find the courage within yourself to withstand this pain and difficulty. When you start achieving small personal victories, your confidence and courage grow, and along with them, your self-discipline grows. **5. Inner self-talk.** Internal dialogue can often be harmful, but it can also be helpful if you know how to control it. When facing challenges, talk to yourself, encourage and reassure yourself. After all, internal dialogue allows you to remind yourself of your goals, summon courage, support yourself, and help you become aware of tasks. Remember one quote: "The price of self-discipline is always less than the pain of regret." You can write it down and use it in your inner self-talk.

title: 5 business principles that every entrepreneur should know
text: **1. Value: what the client pays for.** Business exists to create value of various kinds. It takes raw materials and labor resources and adds value to them in some way by transforming them into goods or services that are subsequently purchased by customers. Value is what customers pay for. For example, McDonald's creates customer value by creating places where people can eat inexpensively while away from home. The company builds restaurants, hires chefs and people to serve customers, buys meat and prepares food. Customers appreciate the convenient location (no need to go home to eat) and the taste of the food (most people like hamburgers, chicken dishes, soft drinks and fries). **2. Let's get organized.** Any organization must have a good organization! It must have goals and resources (human, material and financial) to achieve these goals. The organization must track the implementation of all projects and the results obtained. Each department must perform its functions properly. Each employee must be assigned tasks that serve the goals of the organization. **3. Competitive advantage: winner's wreath.** To succeed in its market, a company must do something better than other players. Producing that something better creates a competitive advantage. That something can only be one aspect of a product or service as long as customers value that aspect highly. For example, a company can achieve a competitive advantage by offering the widest range of products. Or super low prices. Or high quality. Or great service. But you can't achieve all this at once. **4. Control is something you should never lose.** Once management decides how the company will create customer value, organize the business, and enhance competitive advantage, it must take control of the firm. This does not necessarily imply management with an iron fist (although some managers believe so). Rather, it means that everyone should be aware of the company's goals and given assignments that will move the company toward those goals. **5. Profitability: you must have it.** Business exists to make money. Money earned in a business can be counted in several ways. But no matter how they are calculated, a business must make money - make a profit from its operations. If, over a period of time, a business makes more money from its activities than it spends on its activities, it is said to make a profit for that period. If not, he suffers losses. A company cannot sustain losses for a long time, otherwise it goes bankrupt.

title: 5 mistakes new startups make
text: 1. Pursue the initial idea. 90% of startups that reach exit did so with a different idea than they started with. 2. Look for a niche with low competition. If there are no competitors, it means there is no money. 3. Put a low price on your product. Maybe you just feel the product lacks value? 4. Accelerate development, not sales. Don't sell what you develop, but develop what sells. 5. Talk to those who bought and not to those who did not buy. If one out of a thousand clicks on an advertisement, and one out of a hundred site visitors buys, then the margin of growth is in the understanding of those who are not attracted to your offer.

title: How to properly present a project to an investor?
text: **1. Explain what you do.** Talk about what you're doing as early as possible. Preferably in the first sentence. **2. Get to the demo quickly** Demonstrating a product will give you a better idea of it than anything you can say. **3. A short description is better than a lengthy one.** Your initial goal is not to talk about all future development opportunities, but to let investors know that you are worth talking to further. **4. Don't do everything at once** Have one person give the presentation while the other sits at the computer and switches slides. While you are standing in front of an audience, they will listen to you, at least out of politeness. **5. Don’t talk for a long time about unimportant things** If you only have a few minutes, spend them explaining what your product can do and why it's great. **6. Don't go too deep into the business model.** This is not what investors want to hear during a short presentation. Plus, the business model you have now is probably wrong. **7. Speak slowly and clearly in front of an audience.** If you feel like you're speaking too slowly, you're speaking at the right speed. **8. Let only one speak** Startup founders often like to emphasize that all partners in the company are equal. This is a good sign. Investors don't like it when teams are discordant. But there is no need to show this at the presentation, speaking in turns. It's distracting. **9. Appear confident** That is, you need to look confident, and not talk about it. There is no point in declaring that “we are firmly convinced” or “our product is incomparable.” If you've created something really good, then you honor investors by telling them about it. **10. Don't try to appear better than you are.** You just have to convince investors that you are smart and ready for something bigger. If you try too hard to hide your immaturity—for example, by trying to reason about things you don't know—you may be hiding your talents. Investors can easily spot a faker. **11. Don't write long captions for slides** If your slide captions are too long, people simply won't read them. **12. Hard numbers look convincing.** If you have specific data, even preliminary, share it with the public. The numbers are easy to remember. If you can state that on average each visitor views a page 12 times, state it. But you should not report more than 4-5 figures per presentation. And all the numbers should characterize your project directly. There is no need to talk about the size of the market in which you are going to work. **13. Tell real user stories** It's very helpful to talk about problems that specific users encountered and how you solved them. Or better yet, tell us how you yourself encountered an obstacle and got around it. You can also give examples of people you know personally - family or friends. **14. Come up with a keyword phrase** Write and learn a short key phrase that will stick in the heads of your listeners.

title: How to delegate authority correctly
text: The art of management is achieving results through the efforts of other people. And delegation of authority is one of the main skills of an effective leader. Brian Tracy, a well-known expert on efficiency and the psychology of success, has come up with a golden formula that will help you correctly delegate authority to subordinates. It includes 7 principles. **1. The level of the task must correspond to the level of the performer** Remember a simple rule: if a person can complete 70% of a task, he can be entrusted with it entirely. And if the task is completely new, correlate its complexity with the skills, abilities and level of motivation of the person to whom you plan to entrust it. It is important that the work is not too difficult and that the person can cope with it. **2. Delegate gradually** Transfer authority gradually, developing self-confidence in the person. Obviously, you want to “harden” it from the very beginning by loading it with many small tasks. But when the cases are larger and more serious, the delegation process must be gradual. **3. Delegate the entire task** One of the main motivators in the business environment is the feeling of full responsibility for the assigned task. 100% responsibility engenders confidence, competence and self-respect. Each of your employees, no matter what position they hold, should have at least one function for which they are entirely responsible. If he doesn't do the job, no one else will do it for him. **4. Expect a specific result** Think about what specific outcome you want to achieve when delegating. Help your subordinates clearly understand what you expect from them in the end. Be sure to ask again how the person understood the task and what is expected of him. **5. Encourage participation and discussion** There is a direct correlation between discussion and interest in getting the job done. When people have the opportunity to communicate directly with management, their desire to do a good job increases. **6. Delegate authority and responsibility** Delegate authority commensurate with the level of responsibility. If the task is large, let employees know how much time will be allocated to it and who they can contact for additional help. A common mistake managers make is underestimating what employees might need to do a good job, be it time or money. **7. Leave the performer alone** Let the subordinate bear 100% responsibility. Don't take the task back. You may, without realizing it, take it back by constantly checking in with the employee, demanding accountability, and suggesting changes and adjustments to the process. The ability to delegate a task is a key factor in a leader's success. With the right delegation, your potential is virtually limitless. Without this skill, you will be forced to do everything yourself.

title: 7 Ways to Develop Perseverance
text: **1. Study the lives of successful people.** Understanding that perseverance has helped many achieve success will inspire you to develop this quality in yourself. Find and read biographies of successful people. While most only focus on their achievements, focus your attention on their perseverance that allowed them to achieve their goals. **2. Find partners and like-minded people.** It will be easier to achieve success if you are surrounded by partners and like-minded people who support you.
